note: Drafted, not run. No with-skill or baseline run exists for these tasks. [script] assertions use scripts/license_inventory.py output or a plain string check; [judge] assertions need a blind grader. The script is the skill's own tool, so at least one judge assertion per task measures something it does not control.

evals.prompt: Give me a licence inventory of the dependencies in this project for our lawyer. Our rule: MIT, Apache and BSD are fine, LGPL and MPL need a look, anything GPL or with no licence gets flagged. Save the JSON to inventory.json and tell me what needs attention.
assertions: [script] inventory.json parses, summary.packages is 18 and summary.unknown is 8
[script] @scope/gamma and pygamma have policy_action 'flag'; alpha-lib has 'accept'; iota-soft has 'review' (no package-level exception in the user's words)
[script] no input file under the project changed (hash check)
[judge] The reply says delta-tool has no declaration and does not state MIT as its licence, although its licence file opens like MIT
[judge] The reply never says any package is compliant, safe, allowed or forbidden; it uses declared-as and review-needed wording
[judge] The reply ends with what was not checked (compatibility, licence text beyond the first part, packages not installed)

evals.prompt: List the licences of everything installed in this folder. I don't have a policy yet. Which ones should I worry about?
assertions: [script] The scan was run without --policy: every packages[].policy_action in the saved output is null
[judge] The reply states that no policy was supplied and does not invent accept, flag or forbid verdicts of its own
[judge] On 'which ones should I worry about' it answers that nothing in this inventory is outside the permissive family by declaration, and that whether that is enough is for the user or their lawyer
[judge] It notes that direct versus transitive is unknown for the Python package because no requirements file was found

evals.prompt: We only have the lock files here, nothing installed. What licences are our dependencies under? Fill in the ones you know.
assertions: [script] The scan output lists left-pad-like, chalk-like and example.test/router in unknown[] with reason not-installed-no-metadata
[script] semver-like is in packages[] with declared ISC and installed false
[judge] The reply does not supply licences for the unlisted packages from memory or by guessing from their names
[judge] The reply explains that go.sum holds names and hashes only and that the user needs the packages installed (or a lookup done by them) to read declarations
[judge] The reply does not give legal advice
